conclusion: The alleged memcpy overlap was a mistaken conflation of two sequential memcpy calls. With source and destination views backed by the same buffer, neither individual memcpy call has overlapping source and destination byte ranges. No W6RC-001 blocker remains.

exact_implementation.offset_0x40_case: For the final record store, source_offset and destination_offset are both 0x40. The read call copies B[0x40..0x44) into local word; only after it returns, the write call copies local word back to B[0x40..0x44). Those ranges coincide across two different calls, not within either call; this is defined ordered load-then-store behavior.

exact_test_oracle.finding: apply_expected uses the same two-call local-word staging as production. Its source and destination pointers are equal at the view level, but each individual memcpy pairs the external array with a separate local uint32_t. Therefore the oracle's +0x40 case is also defined.
